references.title: Aircraft Overview: Gulfstream G650/G650ER
references.author: Aviation Week
references.scope: Secondary: cabin width 2.49 m, height 1.91 m.

calibration: No drawing found. 57 px/m along the body from 30.41 m, 54 px/m in height from 7.82 m; the difference is consistent with the view being yawed.

comparisons: Side render stacked above the photograph and inspected. Three-quarter render inspected. No overlay was made because the photograph is yawed.
corrections: Row width corrected from 2.59 to 2.70 m: 2.59 m leaves no wall around the 2.49 m finished cabin, and the depth reads 2.7 m at the height-derived scale.
Oval windows replaced an octagon that read as diamonds at distance.
Wing built from the published 36 degree sweep and 119.2 m2; the photographed tip position then matches once the 20 degree yaw is allowed for.
Seated eye moved from u 3.85 to 2.95 and h 2.00, placed as on the Dash 8 and CJ4. No published eye position was found, so this is an estimate.
Sill lowered about 0.05 m; the first pillar's upper end moved aft to 2.60 so it stays outboard of the pilot.

Kit changes: glass clear from the seat and tinted from outside, as on the Bendy airliner. The thick glareshield slab and its large FLIGHT GUIDANCE lettering are replaced by a thin sloped hood with a rolled lip over a slim mode control strip. The panel, floor and overhead take their reach from the nose skin, and a dark coaming lines the inside of the nose.

limitations: Lowest-confidence group: no dimensioned drawing. External fuselage width, wheelbase, track and tail span are inferred, not sourced.
The two photograph scales disagree by 5 percent; window spacing would suggest the lower one. Stations along the body may be off by that margin.
Height runs slightly over the published figure. Flight deck and cabin door details are not type-reviewed.
Exterior only: shared interior, refitted but not compared with a PlaneView flight deck.
Eye station and window limits are estimated, not measured.
Sanity pass only: seating, glass and visibility. The panel, hood and pedestal remain the shared kit interior fitted to the nose, not compared with this type's real flight deck.
